audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed as Eliphaz's second speech: accusation that Job's words are wind, appeal to ancient wisdom, human impurity claim, and vivid fate-of-the-wicked imagery. Marked as Eliphaz's speech, not final theology.

verses.restored: Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said:

familiar.text: Then answered Eliphaz the Temanite, and said,

verses.restored: Should a wise person answer with knowledge of wind and fill his belly with the east wind?

familiar.text: Should a wise man utter vain knowledge, and fill his belly with the east wind?

verses.restored: Should he argue with speech that does not profit, with words that do no good?

familiar.text: Should he reason with unprofitable talk? or with speeches wherewith he can do no good?

verses.restored: Indeed, you break down fear and diminish meditation before the Divine.

familiar.text: Yea, thou castest off fear, and restrainest prayer before God.

verses.restored: For your guilt teaches your mouth, and you choose the tongue of the crafty.

familiar.text: For thy mouth uttereth thine iniquity, and thou choosest the tongue of the crafty.

verses.restored: Your own mouth condemns you, not I; your own lips testify against you.

familiar.text: Thine own mouth condemneth thee, and not I: yea, thine own lips testify against thee.

verses.restored: Were you the first human born? Were you brought forth before the hills?

familiar.text: Art thou the first man that was born? or wast thou made before the hills?

verses.restored: Do you listen in the council of the Divine? Do you limit wisdom to yourself?

familiar.text: Hast thou heard the secret of God? and dost thou restrain wisdom to thyself?

verses.restored: What do you know that we do not know? What do you understand that is not with us?

familiar.text: What knowest thou, that we know not? what understandest thou, which is not in us?

verses.restored: Both the gray-haired and the aged are among us, older than your father in days.

familiar.text: With us are both the grayheaded and very aged men, much elder than thy father.

verses.restored: Are the comforts of the Divine too small for you, and the gentle word with you?

familiar.text: Are the consolations of God small with thee? is there any secret thing with thee?

verses.restored: Why does your heart carry you away, and why do your eyes flash,

familiar.text: Why doth thine heart carry thee away? and what do thy eyes wink at,

verses.restored: that you turn your spirit against the Divine and bring such words out of your mouth?

familiar.text: That thou turnest thy spirit against God, and lettest such words go out of thy mouth?

verses.restored: What is a mortal, that he should be clean, or one born of woman, that he should be righteous?

familiar.text: What is man, that he should be clean? and he which is born of a woman, that he should be righteous?

verses.restored: Look, he puts no trust in his holy ones, and the heavens are not clean in his eyes;

familiar.text: Behold, he putteth no trust in his saints; yea, the heavens are not clean in his sight.

verses.restored: how much less one who is abominable and corrupt, a human who drinks injustice like water!

familiar.text: How much more abominable and filthy is man, which drinketh iniquity like water?

verses.restored: I will show you; hear me. What I have seen, I will recount,

familiar.text: I will shew thee, hear me; and that which I have seen I will declare;

verses.restored: what wise people declare and did not hide from their fathers,

familiar.text: Which wise men have told from their fathers, and have not hid it:

verses.restored: to whom alone the land was given, and no stranger passed among them.

familiar.text: Unto whom alone the earth was given, and no stranger passed among them.

verses.restored: All his days the wicked one writhes, and numbered years are stored up for the ruthless one.

familiar.text: The wicked man travaileth with pain all his days, and the number of years is hidden to the oppressor.

verses.restored: Sounds of dread are in his ears; in peace a destroyer comes upon him.

familiar.text: A dreadful sound is in his ears: in prosperity the destroyer shall come upon him.

verses.restored: He does not believe he will return from darkness, and he is watched for by the sword.

familiar.text: He believeth not that he shall return out of darkness, and he is waited for of the sword.

verses.restored: He wanders for bread, saying, Where is it? He knows a day of darkness is ready at his hand.

familiar.text: He wandereth abroad for bread, saying, Where is it? he knoweth that the day of darkness is ready at his hand.

verses.restored: Distress and anguish terrify him; they overpower him like a king ready for battle,

familiar.text: Trouble and anguish shall make him afraid; they shall prevail against him, as a king ready to the battle.

verses.restored: because he stretched out his hand against the Divine and acted mighty against Shaddai.

familiar.text: For he stretcheth out his hand against God, and strengtheneth himself against the Almighty.

verses.restored: He runs against him with a stiff neck, with the thick bosses of his shields,

familiar.text: He runneth upon him, even on his neck, upon the thick bosses of his bucklers:

verses.restored: because he has covered his face with fat and gathered fat on his loins.

familiar.text: Because he covereth his face with his fatness, and maketh collops of fat on his flanks.

verses.restored: He dwells in ruined cities, in houses no one inhabits, which are ready to become heaps.

familiar.text: And he dwelleth in desolate cities, and in houses which no man inhabiteth, which are ready to become heaps.

verses.restored: He will not become rich; his wealth will not endure, and their possessions will not stretch over the earth.

familiar.text: He shall not be rich, neither shall his substance continue, neither shall he prolong the perfection thereof upon the earth.

verses.restored: He will not depart from darkness; flame will dry up his shoots, and by the breath of his mouth he will depart.

familiar.text: He shall not depart out of darkness; the flame shall dry up his branches, and by the breath of his mouth shall he go away.

verses.restored: Let him not trust in emptiness, deceiving himself, for emptiness will be his exchange.

familiar.text: Let not him that is deceived trust in vanity: for vanity shall be his recompence.

verses.restored: Before his day it will be fulfilled, and his branch will not be green.

familiar.text: It shall be accomplished before his time, and his branch shall not be green.

verses.restored: He will shake off his unripe grape like the vine, and cast off his blossom like the olive tree.

familiar.text: He shall shake off his unripe grape as the vine, and shall cast off his flower as the olive.

verses.restored: For the company of the godless is barren, and fire consumes the tents of bribery.

familiar.text: For the congregation of hypocrites shall be desolate, and fire shall consume the tabernacles of bribery.

verses.restored: They conceive trouble, give birth to harm, and their belly prepares deceit.

familiar.text: They conceive mischief, and bring forth vanity, and their belly prepareth deceit.
